answer: Autonomous agents managing jade quarries, lotus wetlands, and orchard microclimates mitigate Sybil attacks using collateralized peer vouching. Entering the network requires an existing member to stake bonded tokens on the recruit, which are slashed if fraud occurs. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking and risking genuine capital per counterfeit agent. However, this dependency restricts open participation and risks forming entrenched cartels among early incumbents.
